heroIntro: Opening a registered official envelope from the National Board of Revenue (NBR) to find a formal Audit Notice under Section 182 or a Show-Cause Notice under Section 212 of the new Income Tax Act 2023 is an alarming experience for any taxpayer. The Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT) questions your declared bank deposits, points to discrepancies between your declared wealth statement and property purchases, challenges source of funds, or alleges unexplained cash credits, threatening punitive tax penalties of up to 200%. Taxpayers often panic, ignoring the notice or paying unregulated intermediaries who make false promises of 'fixing the file.' The Income Tax Act 2023 (Aykor Ain 2023) introduced sweeping modernizations, strict evidentiary standards, and comprehensive statutory appeal rights. Understanding how to structure your written reply, compile lawful asset documentation, and defend your return before the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Taxes Appellate Tribunal is the definitive key to eliminating arbitrary tax assessments.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Answer: What Should You Do If You Receive an Income Tax Audit Notice in Bangladesh?
quickAnswer.text: Under the Income Tax Act 2023 (Aykor Ain 2023), when your tax return is selected for audit under Section 182, or when a Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT) issues a notice under Section 183 or Section 212, you must never ignore the deadline. You must immediately compile an audit dossier containing certified bank statements, registered purchase deeds, loan agreements, audited company financial statements, and previous years' wealth statements (IT-10B). Your tax advocate will draft a formal, point-by-point Written Explanation accompanied by a paper trail demonstrating the lawful source of funds. If the DCT makes an arbitrary or inflated best judgment assessment, you have the absolute statutory right to appeal to the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeals) under Section 285 within 45 days, and subsequently to the Taxes Appellate Tribunal.
highlights: The Income Tax Act 2023 governs all tax audits, assessments, and wealth discrepancy inquiries.
Never ignore a DCT notice; failure to appear results in an adverse 'Best Judgment Assessment' under §184.
Taxpayers can reconcile wealth mismatches using past tax files, bank statements, and family inheritance deeds.
Aggrieved taxpayers can appeal adverse assessments to the Commissioner (Appeals) and Appellate Tribunal.
points: Step 1: Check the statutory section on the notice (e.g., Section 182 Audit, Section 183 Assessment, or Section 212).
Step 2: Note the compliance deadline (typically 15 to 30 days) and apply for a formal time extension if documents need assembling.
Step 3: Prepare a comprehensive documentary dossier reconciling bank inflows with declared income and agricultural/remittance exemptions.
Step 4: Have an experienced tax advocate represent you during the DCT personal hearing or file a statutory Section 285 appeal.

sections.title: The New Tax Landscape Under the Income Tax Act 2023
sections.content:
In June 2023, the Parliament of Bangladesh enacted the historic Income Tax Act 2023 (Aykor Ain 2023), completely replacing the four-decade-old Income Tax Ordinance 1984. The new enactment shifted Bangladesh's direct tax system toward universal self-assessment, mandatory digital reporting, and widespread data cross-matching between the National Board of Revenue (NBR), commercial banks, Sub-Registry offices, and vehicle registration portals.

While universal self-assessment allows taxpayers to file returns smoothly, it expanded the scope of post-filing tax audits. The NBR's automated Risk Management Engine now flags returns exhibiting substantial bank turnover, major real estate acquisitions, or sharp variances in net wealth. When an audit notice arrives, taxpayers often assume the tax officer is accusing them of criminal fraud. In reality, a tax audit is a statutory fact-finding proceeding. Knowing how to present verifiable documentary evidence under the new Act protects your hard-earned assets from arbitrary tax demands.

sections.title: Decoding the Audit Notice: Sections 182, 183, and 212
sections.content:
When you receive a tax notice, the first critical step is identifying the exact statutory section cited by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT). Under the Income Tax Act 2023, tax inquiries fall into distinct statutory categories:

  • Section 182 (Audit Selection): Under Section 182, the NBR or Commissioner selects a return for comprehensive audit based on automated risk parameters. The DCT is legally required to explain the specific risk factors triggering the audit.
  • Section 183 (Audit Assessment): Once selected, the DCT issues notice under Section 183 requiring the taxpayer to produce books of accounts, bank statements, sales registers, and asset purchase deeds.
  • Section 212 (Re-Opening / Escape Assessment): If the DCT discovers that income has escaped assessment, was under-assessed, or that excessive reliefs were claimed in any past assessment year, a notice under Section 212 can be issued to re-open the file within statutory limitation windows.

Understanding which section governs your notice dictates the scope of documents required and the statutory deadlines for compliance.

sections.title: The Dreaded Wealth Mismatch: IT-10B Asset Statements
sections.content:
The single most frequent trigger for tax audit notices in Bangladesh is a mathematical mismatch in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities (Form IT-10B). Under the Income Tax Act 2023, submission of a wealth statement is mandatory for any individual whose gross wealth exceeds BDT 40,00,000, or who owns motor vehicles, or possesses real estate in municipal areas.

Audit notices routinely highlight discrepancies: for example, your net wealth increased by BDT 50,00,000 during the financial year, but your declared business income was only BDT 15,00,000, leaving an unexplained accretion of BDT 35,00,000. In their written reply, the taxpayer must scientifically reconcile this gap: demonstrating non-taxable receipts such as foreign remittances received through formal banking channels (exempt under Schedule 6), agricultural income, capital gains from exempted securities, registered inheritance from parents, or lawful gifts from family members backed by formal tax filings.

sections.title: Unexplained Cash Credits and Bank Deposit Scrutiny
sections.content:
Another primary focus of tax audits is bank account turnover. Under automated data-sharing agreements with Bangladesh Bank's Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU), the NBR receives automated reports of large banking transactions. If your declared business revenue is BDT 30,00,000, but your personal or corporate bank statements show total credits of BDT 1,20,00,000, the DCT will issue a show-cause notice treating the entire BDT 90,00,000 difference as 'unexplained cash credit' and adding it directly to your taxable income under the new Act.

To defeat this presumption, your tax advocate must conduct a detailed bank ledger reconciliation: demonstrating that credits represent business loan disbursements, inter-account transfers between your own accounts, customer advances subsequently adjusted, or funds held temporarily as an agent. Presenting bank statements with clear narration and supporting commercial vouchers successfully dismantles the allegation of hidden income.

sections.title: Drafting the Written Reply and Compiling Evidence
sections.content:
The written response submitted to the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes forms the permanent factual backbone of your tax file. An informal or evasive reply practically guarantees an adverse assessment. A professional tax defense dossier requires:

  1. Point-by-Point Clarification: Address every query in the DCT's notice systematically, cross-referencing specific bank entries, purchase vouchers, and balance sheet items.
  2. Documentary Annexures: Attach certified bank statements, registered property deeds (Saf Kabala), loan sanction letters, audited balance sheets, and copies of previous years' assessment orders.
  3. Citing Statutory Exemptions: Cite specific sections and schedules of the Income Tax Act 2023 and NBR Statutory Regulatory Orders (SROs) confirming the tax-exempt status of specific incomes.
  4. Time Extension Applications: If assembling documents takes longer than the notice period, your advocate must file a formal application under the Act requesting a 15-day extension before the deadline expires, preventing unilateral orders.

sections.title: Best Judgment Assessment Under Section 184
sections.content:
The greatest catastrophe a taxpayer can bring upon themselves is ignoring an audit notice. Under Section 184 of the Income Tax Act 2023, if a taxpayer fails to make a return, fails to comply with all the terms of a notice under Section 183, or fails to produce books of accounts, the DCT is legally empowered to make a Best Judgment Assessment.

In a Best Judgment Assessment, the DCT determines your total income based on their own estimation and available market data, without requiring your consent. The DCT routinely doubles or triples your estimated income, disallows legitimate business deductions, and imposes severe penalties and statutory interest. Once a Best Judgment order is passed, the tax becomes a certified government debt recoverable through bank account freezing under Section 275 and property attachment. Prompt legal representation before assessment finalization is critical.

Taxpayers with no taxable income who still hold an active e-TIN must ensure compliance by filing properly—read our guide on zero income tax return rules in Bangladesh and when to cancel a dormant TIN certificate to avoid future NBR notices.

sections.title: The Appeal Hierarchy: Commissioner (Appeals) & Tribunal
sections.content:
If the DCT passes an arbitrary, unjust assessment order despite your documentary evidence, the Income Tax Act 2023 provides an independent, structured judicial appeal hierarchy:

  • First Appeal to Commissioner (Appeals): Under Section 285 of the Act, any taxpayer objecting to an assessment order can file a formal memorandum of appeal before the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeals) within forty-five (45) days of receiving the assessment order and demand notice. Under the new law, the appellant must deposit ten percent (10%) of the disputed tax before filing. The Commissioner (Appeals) can confirm, reduce, enhance, or annul the assessment.
  • Second Appeal to Taxes Appellate Tribunal: If dissatisfied with the appellate order, the taxpayer can file an appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal under Section 293 within sixty (60) days. The Tribunal is an independent judicial body comprising judicial and accountant members, providing impartial scrutiny of complex corporate accounting disputes.
  • High Court Division Reference: On questions of pure law, the taxpayer can approach the High Court Division under Section 309 of the Act.

sections.title: Illustrative Scenario: Defeating an Arbitrary BDT 25 Lakh Tax Claim
sections.content:
The following illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed) illustrates how an experienced tax advocate resolved an audit dispute in Dhaka:

A commercial importer in Gulshan filed his income tax return under Universal Self-Assessment for the assessment year 2024-2025, declaring a net business income of BDT 28,00,000 and paying BDT 4,20,000 in income tax. Six months later, he received an Audit Notice under Section 182 followed by a Show-Cause Notice under Section 183 from the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (Circle 45, Taxes Zone 2, Dhaka). The DCT pointed out that during the year, the taxpayer purchased a residential flat in Dhanmondi valued at BDT 1,20,00,000, and personal bank accounts showed credit deposits of BDT 85,00,000, proposing to treat BDT 70,00,000 as unexplained investment and demanding BDT 24,50,000 in additional tax and penalties.

The taxpayer retained a Supreme Court tax advocate. The advocate inspected the client's past five years of tax returns and compiled a comprehensive evidence file: (1) bank statements showing BDT 45,00,000 received as a home loan from a private commercial bank; (2) certified proceeds realization certificates (PRC) proving BDT 20,00,000 received as foreign remittance from the taxpayer's brother in Canada (fully tax-exempt under Schedule 6); and (3) previous year accumulated savings. The advocate drafted a comprehensive Written Explanation under the Income Tax Act 2023 cross-referencing each transaction.

During the personal hearing before the DCT, the advocate presented the loan sanction letters and remittance certificates. Confronted with an airtight documentary audit trail, the DCT accepted the explanation, dropped the unexplained investment allegation, and passed an assessment order accepting the declared income with zero additional tax liability, saving the taxpayer BDT 24,50,000 and permanently regularizing his tax profile.

faqs.question: What should I do first if I receive an Income Tax Audit Notice in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Never ignore the notice. Check the specific section cited (Section 182, 183, or 212 of the Income Tax Act 2023) and note the compliance date. Contact an experienced tax advocate immediately to examine your return, bank statements, and draft a formal written response.

faqs.question: Can I get more time to respond to a Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT) notice?
faqs.answer: Yes. You or your authorized tax advocate can submit a formal written application to the DCT requesting a 15-day extension to gather bank statements, deeds, or audited accounts. It must be filed before the original deadline expires.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail to respond to an Income Tax Audit notice?
faqs.answer: Under Section 184 of the Income Tax Act 2023, the DCT can pass a unilateral 'Best Judgment Assessment', estimating your income arbitrarily, disallowing expenses, and imposing heavy taxes, interest, and penalties.

faqs.question: How do I explain a wealth mismatch in my tax return?
faqs.answer: You must provide documentary evidence reconciling the increase in assets, such as formal bank home loans, tax-exempt foreign remittances (with PRC certificates), agricultural income, capital gains, or inheritance and gift deeds.

faqs.question: What is the deadline to appeal an adverse tax assessment in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 285 of the Income Tax Act 2023, you must file a formal memorandum of appeal before the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeals) within forty-five (45) days of receiving the assessment order and demand notice.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay tax before filing an appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals)?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the Income Tax Act 2023, an appellant is generally required to pay ten percent (10%) of the disputed tax before the appeal can be admitted for hearing by the Commissioner (Appeals).

faqs.question: What is the Taxes Appellate Tribunal in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The Taxes Appellate Tribunal is an independent second-appellate judicial authority established under Section 293 of the Act, consisting of judicial and accountant members, that hears appeals against orders passed by the Commissioner (Appeals).

faqs.question: Can an overseas non-resident Bangladeshi (NRB) defend a tax audit from abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes. An NRB taxpayer can authorize a tax lawyer or Income Tax Practitioner (ITP) in Bangladesh through a formal Power of Attorney or Letter of Authority (Form IT-33) to attend hearings and represent them before the tax authorities.
